calls.reason: The Gonen et al. study shows semantic leakage exists in sentence completions, but nothing in the packet measures what share of factual hallucinations it causes, so 'a lot' can't be checked.

The leakage studies show unwarranted associations, and the 2026 follow-up points to a broad associative tendency. Neither separates word-level from concept-level mechanisms, so the 'words rather than concepts' point is unresolved.

This is an open-ended 'never' forecast with no deadline. The 2026 replication found weird generalization brittle and easy to mitigate, but no comprehensive fix or impossibility proof exists either way.

The Roh et al. preprint, public before the post, documents phonetic rewrites of lyrics getting past Suno's verbatim-lyrics filter and producing close melodic and rhythmic matches, including Eminem's Lose Yourself. No independent replication was found.
